# rupaka


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

rupaka (रूपक) means a form, a play that the audience sees, and the figure
of speech that shows one thing through another.

A rupaka demo is one interactive figure that teaches one idea. You write
it as a JSON spec of small blocks: sliders, plots, 3D scenes, flows, and
a gate that asks the learner to predict first. Python checks the spec
([`validate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#validate)),
and a small runtime draws it in the browser with no network. A model can
write a spec for you
([`author`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/agent.html#author)),
because a spec cannot run code.

<figure>
<img
src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vedicreader/rupaka/main/media/parabola.gif"
alt="A learner predicts where the lowest point moves, then moves the slider" />
<figcaption aria-hidden="true">A learner predicts where the lowest point
moves, then moves the slider</figcaption>
</figure>

## Install

``` sh
uv add rupaka        # or: pip install rupaka
```

The headless check
([`check`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/check.html#check)) needs
playwright: `uv add "rupaka[check]"`. It uses the Chromium that
`playwright install chromium` gives, or the browser in
`$FASTCDP_CHROME`. It never runs your everyday Chrome.

## A demo in one minute

Build the spec with the Python builders. You can also write the same
thing as JSON.

``` python
from rupaka.spec import *
```

This demo asks for a sum. The answer and the sliders wait for the
prediction.

``` python
d = demo('sum', 'Add two numbers', ask='Predict the sum before you see it.', state=dict(a=2, b=3), derive=[expr('a + b', 'sum')],
         blocks=[gate('s', 'What is {a} + {b}?', [4, 5, 6], 'sum', why='Say why, in one line.', context='For a = {a} and b = {b}:'),
                 readout('{a} + {b} = {sum}', after='s'),
                 row(slider('a', 'a', 0, 9, 1, lock='s'), slider('b', 'b', 0, 9, 1, lock='s'))])
```

[`validate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#validate)
gives the errors. An empty list means that the spec is good.

``` python
assert validate(d) == []
```

A readout that shows the sum before the gate breaks the think rule, so
[`validate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#validate)
refuses it:

``` python
bad = {**d, 'blocks': [d['blocks'][0], readout('{a} + {b} = {sum}')]}
assert any('wait' in e or 'after' in e for e in validate(bad))
```

`save(d, 'sum.html')` writes one page that works from `file://`. Open it
in a browser. Before the lock in, the sum is hidden. After it, the
learner sees the result and can move the sliders:

## More examples

### Predict, then move a slider

A plot of a curve. The lowest point and the caption wait for the gate,
and the slider is locked until the lock in. The animation at the top of
this page is this demo.

``` python
p = demo('parabola', 'What b does to a parabola', ask='The curve is y = x² + b·x. Now b = 0, so the lowest point is at the origin.',
         state=dict(b=0), derive=[expr('x^2 + b * x', 'curve', over=dict(x=[-5, 5, 101])), expr('-b / 2', 'vx'), expr('-(b^2) / 4', 'vy')],
         blocks=[axis([-5, 5], plot('curve'), point(x='vx', y='vy', label='lowest', after='move'), y=[-6, 10], height=300),
                 gate('move', 'b goes from 0 to 2. Where does the lowest point move?', ['Left and down', 'Right and down', 'It stays'],
                      is_('Left and down'), hides=['vx', 'vy']),
                 slider('b', 'b', -4, 4, 0.5, lock='move'),
                 caption('The lowest point is at x = −b / 2 = **{vx:2}**. Set b to −2. Where does the point go now?', after='move')])
assert validate(p) == []
```

### A 3D scene

A [`scene`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#scene) holds
bodies, forces, labels and camera shots. The force arrow shows the
answer, so it waits for the gate.

``` python
s = demo('lift', 'Twice the weight', state=dict(step=1, cam='wide', w=4), derive=[expr('w * 2', 'up')],
         blocks=[gate('g', 'What is twice {w}?', [6, 8], 'up'),
                 scene(body('base', 'box', [2, 1, 2]), force([0, 1, 0], 'up', on='base', at=[0, 1.5, 0], label='lift, {up}', after='g'),
                       shot(bind='cam'), shot('close:base', step=2), bind='step', steps=['A box.', 'Look closer.'])])
assert validate(s) == []
```

### A worked example and a flow

An explainer (`mode='learn'`) has no gate. It builds one step at a time:
the host moves on with `Rupaka.set(el, {step: n})`. A
[`pair`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#pair) is one row
of a worked example, and a
[`flow`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#flow) is a few
boxes with arrows. `page(panel, theme='paper')` gives the paper look.

``` python
panel = demo('targets', 'Make a question and its answer', mode='learn', state=dict(step=1),
             blocks=[pair(['[18]'], '47', heads=['Input tensor', 'Target'], step=1), pair(['[18, 47]'], '56', step=2),
                     flow([dict(id='g', text='Guess'), dict(id='c', text='Compare'), dict(id='a', text='Adjust')], step=3)])
assert validate(panel) == []
```

width="540"
alt="Two rows of a worked example and a flow of three boxes, on paper" />

of three boxes, on paper</figcaption>
</figure>

### A board with a side panel

`rupaka.board` is the board of the screen guide. A model writes one JSON
line for each mark: a step with a spoken line, marks on the page, and a
side panel.
[`parse_board`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/board.html#parse_board)
checks each line against what the page has. A bad line drops. The model
never sends HTML or script.

``` python
from rupaka.board import parse_board, clean_context
```

The page tells the board its parts (anchors). Here it has one passage:

``` python
text = 'A search engine splits the query into words. It finds the pages that match and makes a ranked list. Then it shows the top results.'
ctx = clean_context(dict(anchors=[dict(id='p1', kind='passage', text=text)]))
```

Each step says one line, marks the passage and adds boxes to a flow in
the side panel:

``` python
lines = """{"op": "step", "say": "First the engine splits the query into words."}
{"op": "underline", "at": {"a": "p1", "text": "splits the query into words"}}
{"op": "panel", "head": "How a search works"}
{"op": "node", "id": "q", "text": "Query"}
{"op": "node", "id": "w", "text": "Words"}
{"op": "edge", "from": "q", "to": "w"}
{"op": "step", "say": "Then it finds the pages that match and makes a ranked list."}
{"op": "circle", "at": {"a": "p1", "text": "ranked list"}}
{"op": "node", "id": "p", "text": "Pages that match"}
{"op": "edge", "from": "w", "to": "p"}
{"op": "node", "id": "r", "text": "Ranked list"}
{"op": "edge", "from": "p", "to": "r"}
{"op": "step", "say": "Last, it shows the top results."}
{"op": "box", "at": {"a": "p1", "text": "the top results"}}
{"op": "node", "id": "t", "text": "Top results"}
{"op": "edge", "from": "r", "to": "t"}"""
board = parse_board(lines, ctx)
assert len(board.steps) == 3 and not board.dropped
```

The page draws it with `rupakaBoard.play(board)`, from the script
`rupaka.board.bundle('js')` and the style `bundle('css')`:

<figure>
<img
src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vedicreader/rupaka/main/media/board.gif"
alt="The board marks the passage and draws a flow in the side panel" />
<figcaption aria-hidden="true">The board marks the passage and draws a
flow in the side panel</figcaption>
</figure>

A panel can also be a table, a list, a faded example with blanks, a card
of a wrong idea, or three stages (see the [board docs](06_board.ipynb)).

### Plain English

[`plain_why`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#plain_why)
finds the parts of a text that are hard to read: long sentences, a
reading grade over 9, semicolons, vague words and nicknames. It needs no
model.

``` python
why = plain_why('The model, which was trained on a very large amount of text from many sources over many weeks, uses attention; it is good.')
assert any('semicolon' in w for w in why) and any('grade' in w for w in why)
```

`plain_errors(spec)` checks all the texts of a demo.

``` python
assert plain_errors(d) == []
```

## Make a demo with a model

`author(concept, ask)` asks a model for a demo, then validates it, plays
it in a headless browser and repairs it. `ask(prompt, sp)` is any
function that sends a prompt and a system prompt to a model and gives
back text. For example, with the `rishi` package:

``` python
from rishi import Chat, resp_text
from rupaka.agent import author
spec = author('compound interest', lambda p, sp: resp_text(Chat('claude/sonnet', sp=sp)(p)))
```

[`author`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/agent.html#author) gives
a spec that passes all the checks, or `None`. See the [agent
docs](03_agent.ipynb) for a live run.

</tr>

`check(spec)` draws the demo in headless Chromium and plays it.

A FastHTML app serves the runtime at a prefix and puts the demo in a
route:

``` python
from fasthtml.common import *
from rupaka.render import Demo, Assets, bundle

app, rt = fast_app(hdrs=Assets('/rupaka'))

@rt('/rupaka/{name}')
def get(name: str):
    kind = {'rupaka.js': 'js', 'rupaka.css': 'css', 'three.js': 'three'}[name]
    return Response(bundle(kind), media_type='text/css' if kind == 'css' else 'text/javascript')

@rt('/')
def index(): return Titled('Add two numbers', Demo(d))
```

A static site can use `save(spec, 'demo.html')`, or put `host(spec)` (a
`div` with the spec in it) in a page that loads `rupaka.js` and
`rupaka.css`.

## More

### How a demo teaches

A demo never shows the answer first. Each demo follows one loop:

1.  Predict. The demo shows the inputs and asks one question. The result
    is hidden.
2.  Reveal. The learner locks in with ⌘↩. The demo shows the result and
    says if the prediction was right.
3.  Manipulate. Now the controls are live. The result changes when the
    inputs change.
4.  Explain. The caption ends with a new question that the learner
    answers with the controls.

The validator enforces step 1: a block that shows a value which the
answer depends on must wait for the gate. An explainer is the one
exception. It has `"mode": "learn"` and no gate, so it shows a thing at
once (see Explainers below).

### What a demo is

A demo is a JSON spec, not code. It has a small state, derived values
from named functions (fns), and a list of blocks. A model can write a
spec safely, because a spec cannot run code.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>part</th>
<th>what it is</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>block</td>
<td>a reusable UI part in <code>rupaka/blocks/&lt;name&gt;/</code>: its
JS, its CSS, a <code>block.json</code> manifest and an example</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>fn</td>
<td>a pure function that computes a derived value: <a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#rules"><code>rules</code></a>,
<a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#rrf"><code>rrf</code></a>,
<a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#softmax"><code>softmax</code></a>,
<a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#lookup"><code>lookup</code></a>,
<a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#expr"><code>expr</code></a>,
<a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#field"><code>field</code></a>,
<code>ids</code>, <code>pick</code>, <code>sort</code>, <a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#fmt"><code>fmt</code></a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>gate</td>
<td>the block that asks for the prediction and hides the result until
the lock in</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>spec</td>
<td>the JSON object: <code>state</code>, <code>derive</code>,
<code>blocks</code> and <code>tables</code>, a <code>mode</code> that is
<code>predict</code> (the default) or <code>learn</code>, and
<code>askable</code> (true by default)</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### The host API

A host page can read and change a demo that it mounted. In these calls,
`el` is the element that holds the demo: the `[data-rupaka]` element, or
the element that you gave to `Rupaka.mount`.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>call</th>
<th>what it does</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>Rupaka.state(el)</code></td>
<td>gives a copy of the input keys (the keys of <code>spec.state</code>)
and their values</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Rupaka.set(el, state)</code></td>
<td>sets the input keys that <code>state</code> has, then runs
<code>derive</code> one time and draws one time. It ignores other
keys.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Rupaka.options(el, gate)</code></td>
<td>gives the option values of the gate <a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#gate"><code>gate</code></a>,
in the order that the gate shows them. Each value is the value itself,
not the text that the gate shows. The gate reads options from the state
after <code>derive</code>, and this call does the same. An unknown gate
gives <code>null</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Rupaka.settle(el, gate, pick, {answer})</code></td>
<td>closes the gate <a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#gate"><code>gate</code></a>
as if the learner picked <code>pick</code>. It draws the verdict and
shows the blocks that wait for the gate. With <code>pick</code> null,
the gate closes with no verdict. An unknown gate does nothing and gives
<code>false</code>. The options object is optional.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Rupaka.open(el, gate)</code></td>
<td>opens the closed gate <a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#gate"><code>gate</code></a>
again, as the Try another button of the gate does. It removes the pick,
the reason and the verdict, and hides the blocks that wait for the gate.
It draws one time. It does not move the focus. A gate that is open does
not change, and the call gives <code>true</code>. A gate that waits for
the host to save a prediction does not open, and the call gives
<code>false</code>. An unknown gate does nothing and gives
<code>false</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Rupaka.mount(el, spec, {save, askable})</code></td>
<td>calls <code>save(state)</code> after each change of an input key.
<code>state</code> is the value that <code>Rupaka.state(el)</code>
gives. <code>askable</code> turns the Ask about this control on or off
(see Host events).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Rupaka.ask(el, text)</code></td>
<td>sends the <code>rk-ask</code> event, as the Ask about this control
does, for example from a voice command. It gives <code>false</code> when
a listener called <code>preventDefault</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Rupaka.append(el, block, {into})</code></td>
<td>adds one block at the end of the demo, or at the end of the <a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#stack"><code>stack</code></a>
or <a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#row"><code>row</code></a>
at the path <code>into</code>, with no rebuild. The parts that show
stay. It gives the path of the new block, for example
<code>'blocks.3'</code>. An unknown block type or a bad
<code>into</code> throws an error.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Rupaka.anchor(el, path)</code></td>
<td>gives the element of the block or the part at <code>path</code>, or
<code>null</code>. Each block has <code>data-rk-id</code>: its path in
the spec, such as <code>'blocks.2'</code>. A part adds to it:
<code>'blocks.2.cells.0'</code>, <code>'blocks.2.to'</code>,
<code>'blocks.3.nodes.1'</code>. The element can be hidden, for example
in a later step.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

`Rupaka.set`, `Rupaka.settle` and `Rupaka.open` never send `rk-predict`,
never add to `st.log` and never call
[`save`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/render.html#save).
`Rupaka.options` only reads. A `lock` does not stop `Rupaka.set`. Each
call throws an error when no demo is mounted in `el`.

To show one demo in two windows, mount the spec in each window. Send
`Rupaka.state` of the first copy to the second window, and call
`Rupaka.set` there. To send a pick, send its index in `Rupaka.options`
of the first copy. In the second window, find the value at that index in
`Rupaka.options`, and call `Rupaka.settle` with it. When the learner in
the first window clicks Try another, call `Rupaka.open` in the second
window.

A host can remove the gate answers from the spec of a copy that a room
sees, so that the room cannot read them early. Then give the answer to
`Rupaka.settle` in `answer`. The gate uses it to draw the verdict.
`answer` is `{is: value}` or a path in the state, as in a gate. When the
spec has an answer, the gate uses the answer in the spec. Rupaka does
not write `answer` into the spec or the state. When the spec has no
answer and you give no `answer`, the gate closes with no verdict.

`rupaka.poll` makes a question for a room from a gate.
`of_gate(spec, gate)` gives the question and the index of the answer.
`public(p)` gives the part that the room sees.

### Host events

A demo sends two events to the host page. Each event bubbles, crosses a
shadow root and is cancelable. In each event, `detail.demo` is the `id`
of the spec.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>event</th>
<th>when</th>
<th><code>detail</code></th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>rk-predict</code></td>
<td>the learner locks in a prediction</td>
<td><a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#gate"><code>gate</code></a>,
<code>picked</code>, <code>ans</code>, <code>ok</code>,
<code>why</code>, <code>context</code> and
<code>settle(saved, message)</code>. A host that saves the prediction
calls <code>preventDefault</code>, then calls <code>settle</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>rk-ask</code></td>
<td>the learner clicks Ask about this, or the host calls
<code>Rupaka.ask</code></td>
<td><code>text</code>: the words of the learner (at most 500 characters,
can be empty). <code>state</code>: the input keys and their values now,
clipped. <code>step</code>: the state key <code>step</code> of an
explainer, else the id of the first open gate, else
<code>null</code>.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

An `rk-ask` event is plain JSON. It never holds derived values, gate
answers, DOM or HTML. A string in `state` has at most 200 characters,
and a list or an object at most 50 items, 3 levels deep. A host that
takes the ask calls `preventDefault`. Then the demo says “Sent to the
tutor.”, else “No tutor is on this page.” For example:

``` js
document.addEventListener('rk-ask', e => { e.preventDefault(); tutor.ask(e.detail); });
// e.detail: {demo: 'add-two', text: 'explain this at b = 2', state: {a: 1, b: 2}, step: 'sum'}
```

The Ask about this control is on by default. A spec turns it off with
`"askable": false`. A host page can turn it on or off for one render,
and the host switch comes first. For example, a talk shows the control
in the editor, but not in the window that the room sees.
[`host`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/render.html#host),
[`page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/render.html#page) and
[`Demo`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/render.html#demo) take
`askable=True` or `askable=False`, which writes `data-rk-askable` on the
element. `Rupaka.mount` takes `{askable}`. The event is the same in
every case.

### 3D scenes

A [`scene`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#scene) block
draws a physical thing in 3D: a jet that hovers, a gearbox, a molecule.
It holds four kinds of part:

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>block</th>
<th>what it is</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#body"><code>body</code></a></td>
<td>a primitive (<code>box</code>, <code>cylinder</code>,
<code>cone</code>, <code>sphere</code>, <code>capsule</code>,
<code>torus</code>) or a <code>group</code>. <code>in</code> puts a body
in another body, so a compound part moves as one. A state key in
<code>rot</code> turns it</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#force"><code>force</code></a></td>
<td>an arrow on a body. Its length is <code>mag</code> times the scene
scale, so arrows compare. <code>mag</code> can be a state key or a
derived key</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#label3d"><code>label3d</code></a></td>
<td>a chip on a point, with a leader line. Chips never overlap: each
chip goes to a free place around its point</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#shot"><code>shot</code></a></td>
<td>a named camera: <code>wide</code>, <code>side</code>,
<code>front</code>, <code>top</code> or
<code>close:&lt;body id&gt;</code>. The scene finds the framing from the
bounds of what shows</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

The scene has a toon look: flat colours in three soft bands, ink
outlines, a soft floor and a contact shadow. The colours come from the
page theme, in light and dark. With `bind`, a scene builds one step at a
time: a part with `step: n` shows from step n, and the camera moves to
the newest shot. With `prefers-reduced-motion`, the camera cuts and
parts show at once. The think rule holds: a force or a label that shows
the answer of a gate must wait for the gate.

rupaka keeps a copy of three.js (0.185.0, MIT) in
`rupaka/static/vendor/three/`. It loads only for a spec that has a
scene, and never from a CDN:

- [`page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/render.html#page),
  [`save`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/render.html#save),
  [`show`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/render.html#show) and
  `md(frame=True)` put three.js in the page when a spec has a scene, so
  the page works offline and from `file://`.
- A server that serves the runtime at a prefix also serves
  `bundle('three')` as `three.js` at that prefix, beside `rupaka.js`.
  The runtime loads it from there the first time that a scene mounts. A
  host that serves it at another place sets `Rupaka.base` before the
  first scene mounts.

#### Scenes and the board

The board of the screen guide speaks one line for each step. It drives a
scene with the host API, so “again”, “slower” and “next” need no new
code:

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>board operation</th>
<th>host call</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>{"op": "step", "n": 3}</code> with a scene spec</td>
<td><code>Rupaka.set(el, {step: 3})</code>, where <code>step</code> is
the <code>bind</code> of the scene</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>{"op": "demo", "set": {...}}</code></td>
<td><code>Rupaka.set(el, {...})</code>, for example a slider value or a
step</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>{"op": "cam", "shot": "side"}</code></td>
<td><code>Rupaka.cam(el, 'side')</code>. It sets the key that a <a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#shot"><code>shot</code></a>
block binds. It gives <code>false</code> for a bad name, or when the
scene has no bound shot</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

`shots(spec)` gives the shot names that a spec knows, so a host can
check a `cam` operation before it draws. Each scene element also tells
its state: `data-rk-shot` is the shot now, and `data-rk-still` is `1`
when nothing moves.

#### Explainers

Sometimes the learner must see a thing before there is a good question,
for example how a jet hovers. An explainer shows a scene at once, with
no prediction step. Set `"mode": "learn"` on the spec. Then
[`validate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#validate)
lets the spec have no gate. All the other checks still run.

- An explainer cannot have a gate, and no block can wait for a gate or
  lock to a gate.
  [`validate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#validate)
  refuses each one and says what to remove.
- With no `mode`, or with `"mode": "predict"`, a spec with no gate is
  refused as before. A `mode` that is not `predict` or `learn` is
  refused.
- The runtime shows a small “Explainer” label above the title, so the
  learner knows that there is no prediction step. The `.rk` element has
  `data-rk-mode="learn"`.

``` python
ex = demo('box', 'A box', mode='learn', state=dict(step=1), blocks=[scene(body('b', 'box', [1, 1, 1]), bind='step', steps=['A box.'])])
```

#### Panels that build with a voice

A board panel shows a worked example one row at a time, while a voice
speaks. Use an explainer with the state key `step`:

- A block with `"step": n` shows when the step is `n` or more, and draws
  in from the left. The host moves on with `Rupaka.set(el, {step: n})`.
- A [`pair`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#pair) is one
  row: input cells, an arrow and the answer, for example `[18] → 47`.
  Its cells come in one by one, 80 ms apart.
- A [`flow`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#flow) is two
  to five nodes with at most eight arrows, in a
  [`row`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#row) or a
  `cycle`.
- A server can stream the panel. It sends the start of the spec, then
  one block at a time. `append(spec, block)` checks each block in
  Python, and `Rupaka.append(el, block)` adds it in the page.
- `Rupaka.anchor(el, path)` gives the element of a part, so the board
  can draw a curve from a mark on the page to that part.
- `theme='paper'` on
  [`host`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/render.html#host),
  [`page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/render.html#page) or
  [`Demo`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/render.html#demo) (the
  attribute `data-rk-theme="paper"`) gives a warm paper ground, light
  boxes, sketch lines and a hand font, Patrick Hand (OFL).

### The screen-guide board

`rupaka.board` is the board of the screen guide. A learner says “I don’t
get X”, and a model answers with a board: one short spoken line for each
step, and marks on the page (a circle, a box, an arrow, a label, a
sketch on a figure) and a small worked example in a side panel. abhyasa
and Leela both use it.

- The model writes JSON lines in a closed language (`OPS`).
  `parse_board(text, ctx)` checks each line against the page context: a
  bad line drops, and two bad lines in a row end the board. The model
  never sends HTML, script or a link.
- `clean_context(raw)` keeps only the known keys of what the page sends
  (its anchors, the focus, the thread and the demo) and cuts them to
  size.
- `stream_board(chunks, ctx, on_step)` gives each step to the page as
  soon as it is whole.
- `static/board.js` draws a checked board as
  `window.rupakaBoard.play(board)`. The side panel is on the paper of
  the demos, in the hand font. A host serves `bundle('js')`,
  `bundle('css')` and the pen libraries in `assets().libs`.

The decisions about learning (when the tutor is sure, which sources to
trust, the prompts) stay in the app.

### Develop

The notebooks in `nbs/` are the source of the Python. The JS and CSS are
hand-written files under `rupaka/static/`, `rupaka/blocks/` and
`rupaka/fns/`.

``` sh
uv sync
uv run nbdev-prepare
uv run pytest
```
